CG Weather Today— छत्तीसगढ़ से दक्षिण-पश्चिम मॉनसून की विदाई का दौर तेजी से जारी है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, प्रदेश के कई हिस्सों से मॉनसून वापस लौट चुका है और अधिकांश क्षेत्रों में बारिश पर पूरी तरह ब्रेक लग गया है। मौसम शुष्क होने से दिन के समय तेज धूप लोगों को बेहाल कर रही है, हालांकि रात के तापमान में धीरे-धीरे गिरावट आने की संभावना जताई गई है।

CG Weather Today: छत्तीसगढ़ में मॉनसून पर लगा ब्रेक, रायपुर समेत कई जिलों में खिली तेज धूप, जानें मौसम का हाल
CG Weather Today
तापमान में बढ़ोतरी, राजनांदगांव रहा सबसे गर्म

वर्तमान में प्रदेश के ऊपर कोई भी मजबूत मौसम प्रणाली यानी स्ट्रॉन्ग वेदर सिस्टम सक्रिय नहीं है। पिछले 24 घंटों के दौरान पूरे छत्तीसगढ़ में बारिश का आंकड़ा शून्य दर्ज किया गया। इस अवधि में राजनांदगांव में सर्वाधिक 35.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस अधिकतम तापमान दर्ज किया गया, जबकि अंबिकापुर में न्यूनतम तापमान 18.0 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, जहां रात में हल्की ठंडक महसूस की जा रही है।

ADVERTISEMENT

मौसम केंद्र रायपुर के अनुसार, राजधानी रायपुर में 5 अक्टूबर को आसमान मुख्यतः साफ रहने का अनुमान है। शहर का अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने की संभावना है। फिलहाल मौसम विभाग की ओर से किसी भी जिले के लिए कोई चेतावनी जारी नहीं की गई है।

इन इलाकों से गुजर रही मॉनसून की वापसी रेखा

मौसम वैज्ञानिकों के मुताबिक, अगले 2 से 3 दिनों के भीतर महाराष्ट्र, विदर्भ और छत्तीसगढ़ के शेष हिस्सों से मॉनसून की पूर्ण वापसी के लिए परिस्थितियां पूरी तरह अनुकूल हैं।

“दक्षिण-पश्चिम मॉनसून की वापसी की रेखा फिलहाल सुपौल, रांची, रायपुर, ब्रह्मपुरी, परभणी, बारामती और हरनाई से होकर गुजर रही है। वहीं, पूर्वी मध्य प्रदेश से होते हुए दक्षिण बिहार से विदर्भ तक एक द्रोणिका (तफ) बनी हुई है, जिससे प्रदेश में मौसम मुख्यतः शुष्क बना रहेगा।”
— मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र, रायपुर

नागरिकों पर असर: दिन में गर्मी, रात में हल्की ठंडक का अहसास

मॉनसून के जाने और बारिश रुकने से आने वाले दिनों में दिन के वक्त तेज उमस और धूप का सामना करना पड़ सकता है। हालांकि, हवा की दिशा बदलने के साथ ही ग्रामीण इलाकों और उत्तरी छत्तीसगढ़ (सरगुजा संभाग) में रात और तड़के के समय हल्की गुलाबी ठंड की दस्तक देखने को मिलेगी। खेती-किसानी के लिहाज से यह शुष्क मौसम धान की फसल की कटाई और सुखाने के लिए अनुकूल माना जा रहा है।

title: Weather Update: 5 अक्टूबर से 10 राज्यों में भारी बारिश का अलर्ट, दिल्ली-UP समेत इन राज्यों में मौसम रहेगा शुष्क - IND24
article_text:
New Delhi | देश के कई हिस्सों में मौसम एक बार फिर करवट लेने वाला है। भारत मौसम विज्ञान विभाग (IMD) के ताजा पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, 5 अक्टूबर से कई राज्यों में बारिश और आंधी-तूफान की स्थिति बन सकती है। मौसम का यह प्रभाव 5 से 7 अक्टूबर के बीच देखने को मिल सकता है। आईएमडी ने केरल, ओडिशा, बिहार, झारखंड, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, गोवा और महाराष्ट्र समेत दक्षिण भारत के कुछ हिस्सों में बारिश की संभावना जताई है। कुछ क्षेत्रों में गरज-चमक के साथ तेज हवाएं चलने का भी अनुमान है।
5 से 7 अक्टूबर तक बारिश का दौर
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, 5 अक्टूबर से 7 अक्टूबर के बीच देश के कई हिस्सों में बारिश की गतिविधियां बढ़ सकती हैं। खासतौर पर पूर्वी, मध्य, पश्चिमी तट और दक्षिण भारत के कुछ हिस्सों में मौसम सक्रिय रहने की संभावना है। बारिश के साथ कुछ स्थानों पर आंधी और गरज-चमक की स्थिति भी बन सकती है। स्थानीय स्तर पर बारिश की तीव्रता अलग-अलग रह सकती है।
इन राज्यों में बारिश और आंधी-तूफान के आसार
आईएमडी के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक केरल, ओडिशा, बिहार, झारखंड, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, छत्तीसगढ़, गोवा और महाराष्ट्र के कई हिस्सों में बारिश की संभावना है। दक्षिण भारत के कुछ अन्य राज्यों में भी मौसम सक्रिय रह सकता है। इन क्षेत्रों में रहने वाले लोगों को मौसम विभाग के स्थानीय अपडेट पर नजर रखने की सलाह दी गई है, खासकर बारिश और गरज-चमक के दौरान खुले स्थानों पर सावधानी बरतने की जरूरत होगी।
दिल्ली-NCR, हरियाणा और यूपी में कैसा रहेगा मौसम?
आईएमडी के मुताबिक दिल्ली, हरियाणा, चंडीगढ़ और उत्तर प्रदेश में इस अवधि के दौरान मौसम के अपेक्षाकृत शुष्क रहने की संभावना है। यानी 5 से 7 अक्टूबर के बीच इन क्षेत्रों में देश के बारिश प्रभावित राज्यों की तुलना में व्यापक बारिश की संभावना कम है। हालांकि, स्थानीय मौसम में बदलाव संभव है और शहरवार पूर्वानुमान अलग हो सकता है।
लोगों को मौसम अपडेट पर नजर रखने की सलाह
बारिश और आंधी की संभावना वाले राज्यों में लोगों को स्थानीय प्रशासन और मौसम विभाग की ओर से जारी ताजा चेतावनियों का पालन करने की सलाह दी जाती है। विशेष रूप से गरज-चमक के दौरान खुले मैदान, पेड़ और कमजोर ढांचों से दूरी बनाए रखना सुरक्षित रहेगा।

title: Financial aid to flood-hit people delayed as I won’t let Akhil Gogoi take credit for it: Himanta - The Meghalayan Express
article_text:
ASSAM
2 min.Read
Financial aid to flood-hit people delayed as I won’t let Akhil Gogoi take credit for it: Himanta
By
TME
October 5, 2026

Guwahati, Oct 5 (PTI) Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Sunday said the disbursement of financial assistance to flood-hit people in the eastern districts was being delayed so that opposition MLA Akhil Gogoi cannot claim credit for the release.

Gogoi, the Raijor Dal president, has been staging an indefinite sit-in on the state assembly premises here for the last three days seeking quick disbursement of the aid. He accused the chief minister of politicising the issue and trying to make light of a grave situation, noting that barring a few families, a majority of the affected people have not received any financial assistance from the government.

“Around seven days ago, Gogoi had spoken to me over the phone at length on the compensation issue… I had explained to him in detail. Now, when he knows that people will get the money, he wants to take the credit. We have to delay the disbursement so that he cannot claim the credit,” Sarma said at a press conference here.

“My mistake was sharing with him details about the compensation. He is indulging in politics over the matter, and so will I,” the CM added.Government

Sarma claimed the people have lost faith in Gogoi.

“Gogoi and another person think they can convince the people that they ensured the disbursement of the aid,” he said, without identifying the other person.

He also took a dig at two women opposition leaders for allegedly “hopping from one party’s protest to another” in an attempt to establish their political identity, though he refrained from identifying them.

Gogoi, reacting to the chief minister’s statement, said he was compelled to launch the “indefinite satyagraha” when no help was forthcoming even after 75 days of the devastating floods.

“I sat on protest on October 2, which was the 76th day of the floods hitting the eastern districts. No monetary relief has been extended, barring some families receiving an ex gratia of Rs 15,000 each,” Gogoi told PTI.

“It was a catastrophic disaster and not an annual flood. The way the government dealt with it is unacceptable,” he said.

Gogoi accused the chief minister of politicising the issue and trying to make light of a grave situation.

“I started my protest to remind the government how they have forgotten the people who lost everything,” he asserted.

Among the demands put forth by Gogoi is compensation of a minimum of Rs 10 lakh for each flood-affected family in Sivasagar, Charaideo and Jorhat.

He has also urged the government to provide Rs 15,000 as one-time interim financial assistance to flood-hit people of the three districts, and an additional Rs 10,000 to those in Sivasagar and Charaideo, as announced by the chief minister.

Besides, he also demanded a CBI inquiry into the circumstances leading to the unprecedented floods this year.

At least 108 people died in the floods in the state this year, while houses, schools, roads, embankments, cattle sheds, fisheries and health centres were among the infrastructure damaged in the deluge.

title: Karnataka’s Rainfall Deficit Exposes a Deepening Water Crisis - urbanacres.in
article_text:
Karnataka’s rainfall deficit has reached its worst level since 1971, turning a weak monsoon into a statewide water-governance emergency. Rainfall during the southwest monsoon was 35 per cent below normal, drought has been declared in 177 of the state’s 240 taluks, and the India Meteorological Department has forecast below-normal rain in October and November. The immediate challenge is no longer only agricultural loss. It is whether the state can organise drinking-water supplies through an extended period of hydrological stress.

The scale of the shortfall is evident across every month of the southwest monsoon. Karnataka received around 40 per cent less rain than normal in June, with 130 mm recorded against a normal of 215 mm. July rainfall was 29 per cent below normal at 192 mm compared with 271 mm, while August recorded 169 mm against a normal of 220 mm, a deficit of 23 per cent. September was the weakest month, with rainfall 54 per cent below normal: 74 mm against the usual 161 mm.

This cumulative pattern matters more than any single monthly number. A late-season recovery could have reduced the annual deficit, but September instead deepened it. The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre has identified this as the state’s worst southwest monsoon performance since 1971. The previous highest deficit was recorded in 2002, when rainfall was 33 per cent below normal. The comparison places the current season within a long record of severe rainfall failures rather than treating it as an isolated spell of bad weather.

The shortage has also been geographically uneven. In September, the rainfall deficit reached 69 per cent in Malnad, 65 per cent in coastal districts and 61 per cent in North Karnataka. These regions differ in their physical geography, settlement patterns and water systems, but the figures point to a common administrative problem: water planning cannot rely on a single statewide average when local rainfall conditions are diverging sharply.

For the state’s water systems, the next stage will be defined by what remains available after the monsoon has ended. Rainfall is one input, but drinking-water security depends on the condition of groundwater, the performance of local supply infrastructure, the availability of storage and the ability of authorities to move water to places where local sources fail. The government’s response has therefore focused on gathering groundwater information across all 5,927 gram panchayats and preparing an action plan extending until the next monsoon.

That administrative instruction is significant because it shifts the problem from emergency response to system-wide monitoring. The government has already declared drought in 177 of 240 taluks, with more areas expected to be added. Officials have been asked to ensure adequate drinking water in the coming months, while a meeting chaired by Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre noted that the number of areas facing water shortages was increasing daily.

The reference to all 5,927 panchayats also reveals the scale at which the state must plan. A drought declaration is made at the taluk level, but drinking-water problems are experienced at the settlement and household level. Panchayats are the operational units through which local conditions, groundwater availability and supply requirements must be compiled. Without that granular picture, statewide rainfall data can identify the severity of the season but cannot by itself determine which communities require tankers, source augmentation or alternative supply arrangements.

The distinction between rainfall deficit and drinking-water shortage is central to understanding the crisis. A deficit of 35 per cent does not mean that every location has lost exactly 35 per cent of its usable water. It is an indicator of reduced rainfall against the normal level. The effect on people depends on where rain fell, how much water entered local storage and aquifers, and how effectively existing supply systems can carry available water to demand centres. The supplied data establishes the rainfall shortfall and the growing number of affected regions, but does not provide a state-level inventory of reservoirs, groundwater levels or household supply interruptions.

That missing information is precisely why the proposed groundwater compilation is important. Groundwater data across every panchayat can help authorities distinguish areas where sources remain viable from those where wells and borewells are under pressure. It can also make drought planning more specific. However, the source material does not establish how frequently the data will be updated, how it will be shared with local administrations or what funding has been assigned for implementation. Those details will determine whether the exercise becomes a functioning monitoring system or remains a one-time assessment.

The forecast for October and November adds a further layer of uncertainty to the planning cycle. These months are no longer simply a transition between the southwest monsoon and the next agricultural season. With below-normal rainfall expected, they represent an additional period during which drinking-water demand may rise while natural replenishment remains limited. The state must therefore prepare for a period that extends beyond the formal end of the monsoon season.

Karnataka’s institutional response is spread across multiple levels. The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre provides the rainfall assessment. The IMD supplies the forecast. The state government determines drought declarations, while the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj administration is directing local officials to prepare water-supply plans and compile groundwater information through the panchayat network. This division of responsibilities is necessary, but it also means that information must move reliably from monitoring agencies to district and taluk administrations and then to local supply operations.

The current figures show why that chain matters. A state-wide deficit can become a local emergency when several pressures overlap: a weak monsoon, a highly deficient September, a forecast of continued below-normal rain and a rising number of regions reporting drinking-water shortages. The declaration of drought across 177 taluks provides an administrative framework for response, but the operational test will be whether the framework reaches the 5,927 panchayats where water sources and daily demand have to be assessed.

The data also complicates the idea that the crisis is confined to one part of Karnataka. Malnad, coastal Karnataka and North Karnataka recorded particularly severe September deficits, while the source states that rainfall was deficient in all four months across the state. The drought declaration covering 177 taluks reinforces that the problem is broad-based, even though the severity and local consequences will vary.

For cities and larger towns, the implications are connected to the same rural and local-government systems. The supplied report does not quantify urban shortages or identify specific city reservoirs, so no city-level conclusion can be drawn from the available evidence. But the government’s focus on drinking-water availability until the next monsoon establishes that the challenge extends beyond farm rainfall. Urban and rural supply planning will have to be understood as part of a wider state water system in which weakened local sources can increase pressure on public authorities.

The immediate policy question is therefore not only how Karnataka responds to a record rainfall deficit, but how it converts rainfall information into reliable water decisions. The evidence confirms that the state has entered a severe drought-management phase: rainfall was 35 per cent below normal, September was exceptionally deficient, 177 taluks have been declared drought-affected and below-normal rain is forecast for October and November. What remains to be established is the condition of groundwater and local supply infrastructure across the panchayats. The next significant developments will be the completion of that assessment, the addition of any further drought-affected areas and the state’s action plan for maintaining drinking-water supplies until the next monsoon.

title: Monsoon Retreat Triggers 4-Day Thunderstorm Alert Across Odisha - Pragativadi
article_text:
The Regional Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar has issued a Yellow Alert for Odisha, forecasting four days of thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds reaching speeds of 30 to 40 km/h across various parts of the state.

According to the weather bulletin released on Monday, isolated places across Odisha are likely to experience lightning and gusty winds until Tuesday morning.

20 Districts Under Yellow Alert

From Tuesday morning through the morning of October 9, a Yellow Alert will remain active for 20 districts:

Balasore, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, and Kataka

Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Baragada, Sambalpur, Debagada, Anugola, and Dhenkanal

Kendujhar, Mayurbhanj, Subarnapur, Boudh, Nuapada, Balangir, and Kandhamala

Weather conditions are expected to improve from October 9 to October 12, with no formal warnings issued for that period. However, light to moderate rainfall may still occur in a few places.

Cause of the Weather Shift

Dr Sanjeev Dwivedi, a scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, explained that the current weather activity is driven by two trough lines passing through the interior and northern regions of the state during the southwest monsoon retreat phase. This system is bringing light to moderate rainfall along with squally winds across multiple districts. While most parts of the state are currently experiencing dry weather, conditions are expected to change rapidly over the coming days.

Advisory for Citizens and Farmers

The Meteorological Centre has advised the public to take necessary precautions during thunderstorm activity:

Avoid open fields, standing under trees, or staying near water bodies during lightning.

Exercise caution when using electrical appliances during storms.

Farmers are advised to secure harvested crops and provide adequate shelter for livestock.

Stay indoors during warning periods and follow regular official weather updates.

Authorities have urged residents across the affected districts to remain alert and strictly adhere to safety guidelines as the weather pattern unfolds.

title: અમદાવાદમાં વરસાદની બેટિંગ શરૂ, જાણો ક્યાં સુધી છે ભારે વરસાદની આગાહી - Mumbai Samachar
article_text:
Mumbai Samachar
/
gujarat
/
rains-have-started-in-ahmedabad-know-how-long-the-heavy-rains-are-predicted-to-last
અમદાવાદમાં વરસાદની બેટિંગ શરૂ, જાણો ક્યાં સુધી છે ભારે વરસાદની આગાહી
2026-07-04 10:54:00
Author: Mayur Patel



અમદાવાદઃ શહેરમાં લાંબી રાહ જોવરાવ્યા બાદ ગઈકાલથી વરસાદનું આગમન થયું હતું. મોડી રાત્રે હળવું વરસાદી ઝાપટું પડ્યું હતું. જે બાદ આજે સવારથી શહેરના વિવિધ વિસ્તારોમાં વરસાદ પડી રહ્યો છે. અમદાવાદમાં 5 જુલાઈ સુધી ભારે વરસાદની આગાહી છે.
શહેરના કયા વિસ્તારોમાં વરસાદ

અમદાવાદમાં વરસાદની બેટિંગ શરૂ થઈ ગઈ છે. શહેરના બાપુનગર, નિકોલ, નરોડા, ઓઢવ, ઈન્ડિયા કોલોની, સુભાષબ્રિજ, માધુપુરા, શાહીબાગ, દિલ્હી દરવાજા, પ્રહલાદનગર, બોપલ, ઈસ્કોન, શિવરંજની, પંચવટી સહિતના વિસ્તારોમાં ધીમીધારે વરસાદ પડી રહ્યો છે.

અંબાલાલ પટેલે પણ અમદાવાદમાં ભારે વરસાદની કરી છે આગાહી

હવામાન નિષ્ણાત અંબાલાલ પટેલે પણ અમદાવાદ, ગાંધીનગર સહિત અનેક વિસ્તારોમાં ભારે વરસાદની આગાહી કરી છે. અંબાલાલ મુજબ, આજે અને આવતીકાલે અમદાવાદ અને ગાંધીનગરમાં ભારે વરસાદની  શક્યતા છે. વડોદરાના ભાગોમાં ભારેથી અતિ ભારે વરસાદ થવાની શક્યતા છે. ભરૂચ અને મહીસાગર તેમજ સુરતના ભાગોમાં ભારેથી અતિ ભારે વરસાદ થવાની શક્યતા છે. પાટણ, બનાસકાંઠા, અરવલ્લી અને પંચમહાલ જિલ્લામાં પણ સારા વરસાદની શક્યતા વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. સતત વરસાદને કારણે કેટલીક નાની નદીઓ અને સ્થાનિક જળાશયોમાં પાણીના સ્તરમાં વધારો થઈ શકે છે, જેના કારણે પૂર જેવી સ્થિતિ સર્જાવાની સંભાવના પણ છે.

અંબાલાલ પટેલના જણાવ્યા અનુસાર, 8 જુલાઈ આસપાસ બંગાળના ઉપસાગરમાં વધુ એક નવી હવામાન પ્રણાલી સક્રિય થઈ શકે છે. જો આ સિસ્ટમ મજબૂત બનશે તો ગુજરાતના અનેક વિસ્તારોમાં ફરી એકવાર વરસાદનું જોર વધવાની શક્યતા છે.

અમદાવાદમાં કેમ શરૂ થયો વરસાદ

ગુજરાતમાં  અપર એર સાયક્લોનિક સર્ક્યુલેશન, સીઝનલ ટ્રફ, શિયર ઝોન, અને લૉ-પ્રેશર સહિતની વરસાદી સિસ્ટમો એકસાથે સક્રિય થતાં ચોમાસું આગળ વધી રહ્યું છે, જેના કારણે અમદાવાદમાં વરસાદ શરૂ થયો છે.

ગુજરાતમાં સવારે 10 વાગ્યા સુધીના વરસાદી આંકડા

સ્ટેટ ઈમરજન્સી ઓપરેશન સેન્ટર ગાંધીનગર મુજબ, આજે સવારે 6 થી 10 વાગ્યા સુધીમાં રાજ્યના 48 તાલુકામાં વરસાદ નોંધાયો છે. જોકે ચાર કલાકમાં એક પણ તાલુકામાં 1 ઇંચથી વધુ વરસાદ પડ્યો નથી. વલસાડના કપરાડામાં સૌથી વધુ 0.83 ઇંચ વરસાદ નોંધાયો છે. કવાંટમાં 0.59 ઇંચ, ગણદેવીમાં 0.55 ઇંચ વરસાદ પડ્યો છે. 45 તાલુકામાં અડધા ઇંચથી ઓછો   વરસાદ પડ્યો છે.

article_text:
Weather Update | উত্তরবঙ্গে ভারী বৃষ্টির পূর্বাভাস! মহালয়ার আগে আবহাওয়ায় কি বড় বদল আসছে?
ছবি: সংগৃহীত

শেষ আপডেট:

অক্টোবর ৫, ২০২৬

উত্তরবঙ্গ সংবাদ অনলাইন ডেস্ক: অক্টোবরের প্রথম সপ্তাহের প্রথমার্ধে বঙ্গে বর্ষার বিদায় ঘণ্টা বেজে গেলেও উত্তর ও দক্ষিণবঙ্গের আবহাওয়ায় তার রেশ এখনও পুরোপুরি কাটেনি। আলিপুর আবহাওয়া দপ্তরের পূর্বাভাস অনুযায়ী, আগামী কয়েকদিন রাজ্যের বিভিন্ন প্রান্তে বিক্ষিপ্ত বৃষ্টির (Weather Update) সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে। বিশেষ করে উত্তরবঙ্গের পাহাড়ি ও সংলগ্ন জেলাগুলিতে বৃষ্টির প্রভাব কিছুটা বেশি দেখা যাচ্ছে।Local News

সমুদ্রপৃষ্ঠ থেকে ৩.১ কিলোমিটার উচ্চতায় একটি ঘূর্ণাবর্ত উত্তরবঙ্গের আকাশে ঘনীভূত থাকায় জলপাইগুড়ি এবং আলিপুরদুয়ার জেলার দু-এক জায়গায় ভারী বৃষ্টির সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে। পাশাপাশি আগামী বুধবার, ৭ অক্টোবর পর্যন্ত উত্তরবঙ্গের সমস্ত জেলাতেই হালকা থেকে মাঝারি বৃষ্টির সঙ্গে বজ্রগর্ভ মেঘ সঞ্চার ও দমকা ঝোড়ো হাওয়া বইতে পারে বলে সতর্কতা জারি করা হয়েছে। তবে এরপর ধীরে ধীরে উত্তরবঙ্গেও (North Bengal Weather Update) বৃষ্টির পরিমাণ কমবে এবং আবহাওয়ায় পরিবর্তনের ইঙ্গিত মিলেছে।

অন্যদিকে, দক্ষিণবঙ্গের (South Bengal Weather Update) আবহাওয়াতেও চলছে নানা পরিবর্তনের খেলা। ভোরের দিকে কোথাও কোথাও কুয়াশার হালকা চাদর জড়ালেও বেলা বাড়তেই চড়া রোদের পাশাপাশি জলীয় বাষ্পের জেরে অস্বস্তি বজায় থাকছে। বর্তমানে উত্তর-পূর্ব বিহার থেকে ঝাড়খণ্ড ও দক্ষিণবঙ্গের উপর দিয়ে বঙ্গোপসাগর পর্যন্ত প্রায় ৯০০ মিটার উচ্চতায় একটি নিম্নচাপ অক্ষরেখা বিস্তৃত রয়েছে। এর জেরে আজ দুই ২৪ পরগনা, কলকাতা, হাওড়া, হুগলি এবং নদিয়ায় বজ্রগর্ভ মেঘ থেকে হালকা থেকে মাঝারি বৃষ্টির পূর্বাভাস রয়েছে। আগামীকাল এবং পরশু অর্থাৎ মঙ্গল ও বুধবার দক্ষিণবঙ্গের পশ্চিম ও উত্তরের জেলাগুলিতে দমকা হাওয়া সহ বৃষ্টির সম্ভাবনা কিছুটা বেশি থাকবে। তবে ৭ অক্টোবরের পর থেকে দক্ষিণবঙ্গেও বৃষ্টির পরিমাণ ক্রমশ হ্রাস পাবে বলে জানানো হয়েছে।News

ইতিমধ্যেই দেশের উত্তর ভারত সহ গুজরাট, মধ্যপ্রদেশ, বিহার ও ঝাড়খণ্ডের বিভিন্ন অংশ থেকে বর্ষা বিদায় নিয়েছে। রাঁচি, রায়পুর এবং বারামতীর উপর দিয়ে বর্তমানে বর্ষার বিদায় রেখা অবস্থান করছে। আবহাওয়া বিশেষজ্ঞদের মতে, আগামী সপ্তাহের শেষদিকে বঙ্গে পাকাপাকিভাবে বর্ষা বিদায়ের অনুকূল পরিস্থিতি তৈরি হতে পারে। তবে অক্টোবরের দ্বিতীয় সপ্তাহে বঙ্গোপসাগরে নতুন করে একটি নিম্নচাপ সৃষ্টির সম্ভাবনা রয়েছে।

title: IMD Heavy Rain Alert: Storms Likely Across South India - urbanacres.in
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rain in parts of Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Tuesday, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds expected across several other parts of India. The alert covers multiple regions and comes as rain activity is forecast to remain active across the country this week.

Heavy rain is likely at isolated places in Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep may also experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds, according to the IMD forecast.

Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are likely to see thunderstorms and gusty winds, while coastal Karnataka and south interior Karnataka may receive thunderstorms and lightning. The forecast places the southern states at the centre of the immediate heavy-rain outlook, with further rain expected in several areas over the coming days.

In north India, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand may experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Muzaffarabad are likely to see thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds along with isolated to scattered rain. Rain is expected to continue in parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Muzaffarabad in the coming days, while Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand may remain wet through Saturday.

The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms and lightning in Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Vidarbha and west Madhya Pradesh on Tuesday. Gangetic West Bengal may receive thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds. Rain is expected over parts of Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Gangetic West Bengal, sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim during the coming days.

The forecast extends to the northeast and island regions, where isolated to scattered rain is likely in Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The IMD has also indicated that rain may increase in Konkan, Goa and central Maharashtra on Wednesday and Thursday.

The spread of the forecast places roads, public transport operations, outdoor work and local drainage systems across multiple regions under changing weather conditions. The IMD has identified thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds and isolated heavy rain as the principal weather risks in different areas, but the supplied forecast does not specify city-level warnings or disruption advisories.

Rain and thunderstorms are expected to remain active across several parts of the country through the week. The north, east and northeast are likely to continue receiving rain, while the south remains the main focus for heavy rain in the immediate outlook. Rain is also forecast to increase over parts of west India from Wednesday.
